findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_design" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_motion" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_names" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search about 700 real product names - Screenrove's library plus a curated list of products on Mobbin and Refero - each with its domain and TLD, category and der…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: build_recipe, get_motion, get_product, get_screen, pick_reference, search_motion · Private data: build_handoff, build_recipe, get_motion_guidelines, search_logos · Public sink: name_patterns.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: build_recipe, get_motion, get_product, get_screen, pick_reference, search_motion · Private data: build_handoff, build_recipe, get_motion_guidelines, search_logos · Public sink: name_patterns

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "build_handoff" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
